title: Segmented batch pacing with KV-priority lanes to contain looming bursts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Under sustained high QPS spikes we observe repeated short 'looming' bursts that cause: (1) rapid KV cache lane fragmentation, (2) transient GPU OOMs from poor chunking, and (3) long tail latency due to aggressive global hard caps. This ticket proposes a segmented pacing approach: split incoming traffic into priority-aware lanes, apply independent soft/hard micro-batch thresholds per lane, and add an exponential dampening curve for cross-lane token admission to avoid synchronized headroom exhaustion.
design_notes:
- Introduce three KV-priority lanes: control (admin/fallback), interactive (low-latency user), and bulk (background/embeddings).
- Each lane maintains its own microbatch 'soft' target and 'hard' cap. Soft target allows temporary overshoot with linear back-off; hard cap rejects or reroutes to a cheaper model.
- Implement an inter-lane dampening coefficient: when any lane's soft target is breached for >50ms, reduce admission rate for other lanes by a factor computed from current KV fragmentation and GPU free memory.
- Use a rolling 1s histogram of sequence lengths to autoscale per-lane thresholds every 250ms.
- Prefer spill-to-CPU with priority-based eviction for bulk lane before evicting interactive lane entries.
- Maintain compatibility with existing autoscaler and admission-controller hooks; avoid adding synchronous global locks in hot path.
implementation_plan: Add lane metadata to request context and routing layer (ENG: thin header + annotation)
Expose per-lane threshold config in runtime config with sensible defaults (interactive: soft=32/hard=80; bulk: soft=8/hard=32)
Implement per-lane admission token bucket with soft-exceed state and a background dampening reconciler that reads KV fragmentation metrics and GPU free memory
Integrate lane-aware spill policy into KV eviction path with unit tests
Create a simple fallthrough policy to reroute to lower-cost model variant when lane hits hard cap
Add telemetry: per-lane qps, 50/95/99 latency, OOM events, KV hit/miss by lane, and soft->hard transition counts
End-to-end QA on a staging fleet with synthetic looming-burst traffic profile and compare to baseline
acceptance_criteria: No increase in 99th latency for interactive lane under test burst profile compared to baseline (target: <= +5% change)
Reduce cross-lane induced OOMs by >= 90% in staging synthetic test
KV fragmentation metric reduced by >= 30% during bursts
Graceful reroute to cheaper model variant occurs without client-visible failures when hard cap reached
Config knobs exist and can be tuned at runtime without restart
testing_plan: Unit tests for per-lane bucket transitions and dampening math
Integration tests for KV eviction priority (bulk -> CPU -> interactive protect)
Staging workload: replay 10m of production spike traces scaled 3x to validate behavior
Chaos test: randomly kill one GPU and verify inter-lane dampening prevents cascade failures
Regression test against existing admission-controller to ensure no latency regressions on normal traffic
rollout: Canary on 5% of traffic in us-west-2 for 24h, monitor p95/p99 and OOMs. If stable, gradually increase to 50% over 48h. Feature flag guarded (segmented_pacing_v1).
